ceny-paliv-2026-jak-usetrit-na-benzinu-a.title: Fuel prices 2026: How to save on petrol and start earning when you fill up
ceny-paliv-2026-jak-usetrit-na-benzinu-a.seoDescription: Petrol prices rising? Find out how to save on fuel and get cashback every time you fill up. Smart refuelling in 2026.
ceny-paliv-2026-jak-usetrit-na-benzinu-a.content:
In 2026 the world feels like a stormy sea, and drivers in the Czech Republic find themselves right in the eye of the storm. One glance at the price boards outside fuel stations is enough to make many a motorist’s stomach turn. Petrol and diesel prices stopped being mere small talk over a pint long ago; they are now a major item in the family budget, and one that keeps rising relentlessly. Judging by current developments, it is clear that this is no short-term blip you can simply wait out.
While most people spend hours trawling the internet and searching for phrases like “cheapest petrol near me” or “diesel discount”, there is a group of drivers who go about it differently. Smarter. They have stopped seeing refuelling as a necessary evil and started seeing it as an opportunity. Let’s break down what is actually happening on the market and how you, too, can change the rules of the game in your favour.
### Why petrol and diesel prices are rising in 2026
Rising fuel prices are neither a coincidence nor a conspiracy by station owners. They are the result of a complex cocktail of global events brewing thousands of kilometres from the Czech border, yet we taste their bitterness every time we pick up the fuel nozzle.
#### Geopolitics and the price of oil
The Persian Gulf is the energy heart of the planet, and in 2026 that heart is beating irregularly. Any political or military tension around Iran sends immediate ripples through world markets.
•	Brent crude reacts within seconds: Markets hate uncertainty. The moment the first shot is fired or a blockade is threatened, the oil price shoots up.
•	The Strait of Hormuz as a bottleneck: A huge share of global production passes through this strategic point. If logistics slow down, Czech drivers feel it at the pump within 48 hours.
#### The domino effect of rising prices: Why it hurts twice
Expensive diesel isn’t just a problem for owners of diesel cars. It is an engine of inflation. When fuel goes up, road haulage goes up. When transport goes up, you pay more at the supermarket for milk, bread and electronics. This domino effect means that every saving you make on fuel today amounts to protecting your overall purchasing power. A fuel discount is no longer a bonus; it is a survival strategy for expensive times.
### What is the outlook for fuel prices: No stability in sight
Analysts are clear about the rest of 2026: Forget about a return to the prices you remember from previous years. We are in for a period of extreme volatility (fluctuation). One week we may see a slight drop, only for it to be wiped out straight away by a further escalation of the conflict. Sitting back and waiting for “better times” doesn’t pay. The road to savings leads through action, not waiting.
### Petrol and diesel discounts: What people search for most
Czechs are a nation of bargain hunters. As prices rise, Google and the Czech search engine Seznam fill up with queries such as:
•	Where is the cheapest petrol station?
•	Fuel cashback 2026
•	How to save 5 CZK a litre on petrol?
Most of these solutions have one catch, though: they are one-offs. You find a cheap pump on the other side of town, burn fuel getting there, and end up saving nothing at all. A real solution has to be systematic and long-term.
### Smart refuelling: The new standard for 2026
Welcome to an era where refuelling makes sense. The concept of smart refuelling turns the “spend and forget” logic completely on its head. It is no longer about asking: “Where can I save 50 CZK today?” A far more interesting question is: “How can I extract future value from every litre of fuel?” This is where Phmarket enters the story.
### Phmarket: Fuel discounts and rewards for refuelling
Phmarket isn’t just another loyalty card for your wallet that you’ll lose within a week. It is an ecosystem that connects a network of independent fuel stations and gives drivers a tool to fight inflation.
#### An instant discount on fuel
Forget overpriced premium chains that build the cost of their TV adverts into the price. Phmarket works with stations that offer quality without unnecessary marketing. As a result, you get:
•	Prices without the sky-high mark-ups of big corporations
•	A straightforward discount you feel in your wallet straight away
#### Phmarket Coins: A reward that doesn’t run out of steam
This is where the real revolution begins. For every litre you fill up, you earn Phmarket Coins. They are stored automatically in your app. The beauty of it is that you’re not just filling up to get to work. You’re filling up to build your own portfolio of rewards.
•	They’re not just “points for purchases”. They are built on the modern principles of the digital economy
•	Heading for the exchange: Phmarket plans to list these coins on an exchange
•	From user to investor: Fuel turns into a potential asset
### How to save on fuel: A practical guide in 4 steps
Want to join the thousands of drivers who no longer want to simply hand their money over to oil tycoons? It’s easier than you think:
1.	Download the Phmarket app
2.	Find your station
3.	Fill up and collect
4.	Track your progress
### Why does smart refuelling make sense right now?
The year 2026 has taught us that certainty is a luxury. Energy and fuel prices are unpredictable. At times like these, the worst strategy is doing nothing. Phmarket lets you take control. Instead of cursing oil prices in front of the TV, you use a system that gets the most out of every market crisis for its users.
### Summary: Prices are rising, but so is your opportunity
The world has changed, and with it the way we should think about our spending. Prices at the pump may not fall any time soon, but that doesn’t mean you have to lose out.
In 2026 the gap between a passive and an active driver is enormous. The first simply pays up glumly. The second uses Phmarket, saves money, collects coins and calmly watches their everyday running costs turn into an interesting opportunity.
Phmarket: Because your car shouldn’t just swallow money, it should help you make it.

jak-poznat-kvalitni-palivo-kompletni-pru.title: How to recognise quality fuel: The complete guide for drivers (2025)
jak-poznat-kvalitni-palivo-kompletni-pru.seoDescription: How do you recognise quality petrol and diesel? The complete guide: octane and cetane numbers, additives, Czech Trade Inspection (ČOI) checks and tips.
jak-poznat-kvalitni-palivo-kompletni-pru.content:
Fuel quality affects engine performance, fuel consumption, and your car’s reliability and lifespan. Yet most drivers have no idea how to actually tell good petrol or diesel from bad. In this article, we’ll show you step by step how to recognise quality fuel, how to avoid poor-quality fuel, and how the right choice can save you both money and hassle. We’ll also explain why at PHMarket we select partner fuel stations with a strong focus on quality.
1. Why fuel quality matters
- Impact on consumption, performance and engine life
1. What determines petrol quality
- Octane number
- Additives
- Fuel stability and cleanliness
1. What determines diesel quality
- Cetane number
- Biocomponent content
- Winter vs summer diesel
1. How to spot quality fuel at first glance (practical tips)
- Technical condition of the fuel nozzles
- Visible clues at the pump
- Price vs quality (myths and reality)
- How to notice a change in engine behaviour after filling up
1. Poor-quality fuel: symptoms and risks
- Starting problems
- Fluctuating performance
- Clogged injectors and how to clean them
- Water in fuel
1. Fuel quality at PHMarket
- How we select partner fuel stations
- Our fuel quality standards
- Why discounted fuel is still quality fuel
1. Conclusion: quality fuel = savings + a safer engine
#### 1. Why fuel quality matters
Fuel quality is one of the most underestimated factors, affecting not only engine performance but also the long-term running costs of your car. Although most drivers mainly watch the price on the fuel station’s price sign, the real saving isn’t made only at the moment you fill up, but above all in what happens inside the engine afterwards.
#### Quality fuel reduces consumption
Quality petrol or diesel ensures better combustion, faster burning of the mixture and more efficient use of energy. This shows up as:
- lower consumption,
- smoother engine running,
- better response when accelerating,
- stable performance even at lower revs.
An engine often responds to poor-quality fuel with higher consumption, because it has to “make up for” the missing energy content.
#### Quality fuel protects the engine and reduces wear
Fuel that contains the right amount of additives works in your engine’s favour:
- it cleans the injectors,
- prevents deposits from forming,
- limits corrosion of metal parts,
- reduces wear on high-pressure pumps,
- stabilises lubricity (especially in diesel).
With poor-quality fuel, on the other hand, carbon deposits can build up, gradually reducing engine performance and potentially leading to expensive repairs.
#### Quality diesel is crucial for winter driving
In the winter months, fuel quality plays an even bigger role. Low-quality diesel can:
- thicken,
- lose its ability to flow,
- cause cold-start problems,
- put your car out of action in low temperatures.
Quality winter diesel contains special additives that stop it from “freezing”, which is vital for diesel engines.
#### Fuel quality affects both performance and driving comfort
Drivers often describe differences they notice straight away:
- smoother engine running,
- fewer vibrations,
- quicker throttle response,
- less fluctuation at idle.
These differences are not a placebo. They result from differences in octane and cetane numbers, fuel stability, the composition of the biocomponent and the quality of the additives.
#### Fuel quality = long-term savings
Many people feel that fuel quality is an “expensive luxury”. The opposite is true.
Quality fuel:
- extends the life of the injectors,
- reduces the risk of breakdowns,
- prevents poor combustion of the mixture,
- lowers servicing costs,
- helps maintain optimum consumption.
In the end, drivers pay less to run their car than if they regularly fill up with the cheapest fuel of dubious quality.
#### Why PHMarket cares about this
Fuel quality is one of the main reasons PHMarket exists. Our goal is not to offer discounts “at every pump”, but to work only with fuel stations that:
- have offered quality fuel over the long term,
- take good care of their equipment,
- treat customers fairly,
- meet our internal standards,
- maintain consistent supplier quality.
The discount is a bonus. Quality is the foundation.
### 2. What determines petrol quality
Petrol isn’t “just petrol”. Its quality is determined by parameters that directly affect engine performance, consumption, emissions and the lifespan of individual components. The differences between fuel stations are no coincidence: petrol can differ in its origin, storage, additives and even in how well the fuel station is maintained.
Let’s look at the most important parameters that tell you whether petrol is good quality.
#### Octane number: the basic indicator of petrol quality
The octane number indicates how well petrol resists detonation (so-called engine knocking).
The higher the octane number, the better:
- the petrol resists premature ignition of the mixture,
- the engine runs more quietly,
- combustion is more efficient,
- performance is more stable,
- consumption is more predictable.
#### b) What should you fill up with?
In the Czech Republic, you’ll most often find:
- Natural 95 (BA95): standard petrol for everyday cars
- BA98 / 100 octane: for more demanding engines or for smoother engine running
A higher octane rating doesn’t automatically mean more speed. It means a more stable and efficient engine, which anyone who wants to keep their car in good shape will appreciate.
#### Additives: the secret ingredient of quality petrol
Additives are substances that modify the properties of fuel. Although they are rarely talked about, they are essential to petrol quality.
#### Why do they matter?
The right additives:
- improve combustion of the mixture,
- clean the injection system,
- prevent carbon build-up,
- keep the engine in better condition,
- extend component life,
- reduce consumption in the long run.
#### When does it become a problem?
Some cheap pumps sell fuel with minimal additives or with low-quality additives. This can lead to:
- greater injector wear,
- poorer combustion,
- rough engine running,
- higher consumption.
#### Premium vs standard additives
Premium fuels (BA98/100) contain a higher dose of additives, which have both an immediate and a long-term effect. That’s why many drivers feel the difference straight after filling up: the engine runs more smoothly, responds better, and vibrations and jerking disappear.
#### Fuel stability and cleanliness: an often overlooked factor
Quality petrol must not only be well produced but also properly stored and distributed.
#### What affects fuel cleanliness?
1. Condition of the underground tanks: old or clogged tanks can release impurities.
1. Pump maintenance: poorly serviced fuel nozzles can contain deposits.
1. Fuel turnover: a fuel station with low sales may have “stale” fuel.
1. Fuel transport: contamination (water, sludge) can occur even during transport.
Fuel cleanliness has a direct impact on:
- performance,
- injector life,
- the particulate filter,
- smooth engine running.
#### The biocomponent: a source of problems and an advantage
Petrol contains a biocomponent (ethanol), and its quality and quantity have a major impact on the final properties of the fuel.
#### Problems with a low-quality biocomponent:
- it attracts moisture → risk of water in the fuel,
- it makes the mixture less stable when the car stands for a long time,
- it can make starting harder,
- it increases the risk of corrosion of metal parts.
#### What to look for?
Good fuel stations use biocomponents of consistent quality that cause no problems even when the car has been standing for a long time.
#### Conclusion: quality petrol is a combination of parameters
You can recognise truly quality petrol by:
- the right octane number,
- sufficient (and honest) additives,
- fuel cleanliness and stability,
- a quality biocomponent,
- proper fuel station maintenance.
That’s why at PHMarket we only work with fuel stations that meet our quality standards and maintain consistent petrol quality over the long term. The discount comes second. Quality comes first.
### 3. What determines diesel quality
At first glance, diesel looks like a “simple fuel”, but its quality is far more complex than most drivers realise. Modern diesel engines are technologically very sensitive, particularly to fuel stability, biocomponent content, lubricity, cleanliness and the ability to burn at low temperatures.
Quality diesel isn’t just about price. It’s about how well it protects the engine, how reliably it starts in winter, and how cleanly and efficiently it burns.
#### Cetane number: the diesel equivalent of the “octane number”
Just as octane determines the quality of petrol, the cetane number determines the quality of diesel.
The cetane number measures how quickly and smoothly diesel ignites under high pressure.
#### A higher cetane number means:
- quieter engine running,
- quicker engine response,
- better cold starts,
- lower consumption,
- fewer vibrations,
- lower emissions.
#### The standard in the Czech Republic:
- a typical fuel station: 51 to 53 cetane,
- premium diesel: 55 to 60+.
Yes, the difference is noticeable right after filling up. In both older and newer engines.
#### Biocomponent content: the most common problem with Czech diesel
In the Czech Republic, diesel must contain a certain percentage of biocomponent. The problem is that the biocomponent:
- attracts water,
- makes the fuel less stable,
- can increase the risk of injector corrosion,
- lowers resistance to frost in winter.
Low-quality biocomponent = the most common cause of diesel problems.
#### What to watch out for?
- Too high a biocomponent content → poorer cold starts.
- Poor-quality biocomponent → more deposits.
That’s why many drivers look for diesel without a biocomponent, which is more stable, safer for the engine and significantly better in winter.
This type of diesel is very important to PHMarket when choosing partners.
#### Winter vs summer diesel: a huge difference many drivers underestimate
Diesel changes with the seasons.
#### Summer diesel
- thicker,
- less resistant to frost,
- cheaper,
- unsuitable below approx. -10 °C.
#### Winter diesel
- contains additives against paraffin wax,
- gelling point of -20 to -30 °C (depending on quality),
- safe even in severe frost,
- essential for diesel cars in winter.
#### Arctic diesel
- extremely resistant, down to -35 °C,
- used in Alpine regions and by long-haul lorries.
Problems arise mainly at fuel stations that don’t switch to the winter variant in time, and that is where most cases of “frozen diesel” come from.
#### Diesel lubricity: an invisible but crucial parameter
Modern diesel engines have very precise and sensitive components:
- the high-pressure pump,
- injectors (common rail),
- EGR valves,
- DPF filters.
For these parts to work properly, diesel must have certain lubricating properties.
Insufficient lubricity leads to:
- increased wear,
- pump seizure,
- injector failures,
- higher servicing costs.
Quality diesel contains special lubricity additives that minimise these risks.
#### Fuel cleanliness: essential for engine life
Diesel is more prone to contamination than petrol.
#### The most common risks:
- water in the fuel (the biocomponent absorbs it),
- microbial contamination (“diesel bug”),
- sludge in the fuel station’s tanks,
- rust from pipework,
- poor filtration at the pump.
Good fuel stations prevent these problems through regular maintenance and inspections. Unfortunately, some stations neglect maintenance, and the problems only show up once they reach drivers.
#### Fuel turnover: the faster it sells, the better
A fuel station with low diesel turnover = a higher risk of problems:
- fuel instability,
- a greater chance of water or deposits,
- older winter/summer blends.
That’s why it’s safer to fill up where cars come and go frequently.
#### Conclusion: diesel quality isn’t a detail, it’s the foundation
You can recognise quality diesel by:
- a higher cetane number,
- a stable, quality biocomponent,
- the right winter/summer variant,
- high lubricity,
- cleanliness and regular tank inspections,
- fuel turnover.
At PHMarket, we therefore select only fuel stations that consistently meet our diesel quality standards. The discount is an advantage, but what really matters is the certainty of quality fuel that protects the driver’s engine.
### 4. How to spot quality fuel at first glance (practical tips for drivers)
Recognising quality fuel isn’t just about lab tests and technical parameters. As an everyday driver, you have several simple indicators at your disposal that let you judge very quickly whether a fuel station cares about fuel quality, or whether you’d be better off driving a few kilometres further.
Below you’ll find a practical list of tips you can use every time you fill up.
#### 1) Check the technical condition of the fuel station
A clean, well-kept and modern station is usually the first sign that the owner looks after the entire quality chain, from the tanks to the fuel nozzles.
Positive indicators:
- clean floors and surroundings of the fuel dispensers
- well-kept nozzles free of grease and deposits
- modern or regularly serviced dispensers
- a clearly visible, up-to-date price board
Negative signs:
- rust on the fuel nozzle
- drip trays full of dirt and sludge
- peeling paint, old fuel dispensers
- an unpleasant smell around the dispensers
- dirty tanks with visible fuel stains
All of this points to inadequate maintenance, which can also show in the quality of the fuel.
#### 2) Look at the fuel station’s “turnover”
A fuel station where few cars fill up may have:
- old, unstable fuel,
- a higher risk of water in the tank,
- more deposits and microorganisms,
- a slower switch to winter/summer variants.
Turnover matters most for diesel: stale diesel = a higher risk of losing quality.
#### 3) Watch the price, but don’t be fooled
Yes, an extremely low price can be a warning sign. But at the same time, the most expensive fuel isn’t automatically the best.
The rule is this: Price too low → be careful. Normal price → assess other factors. Higher price → often indicates more additives.
So price is an indicator, not a guarantee.
#### 4) Check the fuel nozzles and their condition
Fuel nozzles can reveal more than you might think:
Positive indicators:
- clean nozzles without noticeable grease
- minimal odour
- no dripping after the nozzle is put back
- clean edges and grilles
Negative indicators:
- a greasy, black nozzle
- a smell of old diesel
- dripping after it’s hung up
- visible deposits around the nozzle
This may indicate poor filtration or old fuel.
#### 5) Look at the area around the filters and dispensers
Cleanliness around the dispenser is a sign that the station looks after the hygiene of the whole system.
Positive signs:
- a clean drip catcher
- no large fuel stains
- regularly cleaned grilles and surroundings
Negative signs:
- greasy patches
- sludge under the dispensers
- green or black film (potential microbial growth in diesel)
If the surface is dirty, the system inside is often dirty too.
#### 6) Pay attention to the smell and how the engine behaves after filling up
The engine can be the best indicator of fuel quality:
Positive signs:
- quieter running
- smoother pulling away
- quicker throttle response
- steadier idle
Negative symptoms of poor-quality fuel:
- jerking
- loss of power
- fluctuating idle
- higher consumption
- engine vibration
- harder starting
This usually shows up within 5 to 20 km of filling up.
#### 7) Notice how the station communicates quality
A reputable fuel station:
- states the origin of its fuel
- states the type of additives
- provides information on the winter/summer variant
- displays a contact or a sign about tank inspections
- sometimes even states the quality or the fuel supplier
By contrast, stations that try to stay “completely anonymous” can be risky.
#### 8) Check reviews and long-term reputation
Drivers often share their experiences of:
- harder starting
- problems after filling up
- higher consumption
- poor engine behaviour
Google reviews, car forums and Facebook groups can be surprisingly accurate.
#### 9) When filling up on the road, avoid completely empty stations
If you’re driving through an unfamiliar area and the station is completely empty, and the only one for miles around → better to be careful.
Zero turnover means:
- old fuel
- a higher risk of contamination
- a risk of a poor-quality biocomponent
- irregular deliveries
#### 10) At PHMarket, we check these things for you
Our choice of partners is not random.
Fuel stations in PHMarket must offer:
- consistent fuel quality,
- regular tank maintenance,
- high fuel turnover,
- quality additives,
- a fair approach to customers,
- modern fuel dispensing technology.
Quality is a requirement. The discount is a bonus.
### 5. Poor-quality fuel: symptoms and risks
Poor-quality fuel can cause problems that appear immediately, but often only after weeks or months. Many drivers don’t realise that engine performance issues, higher consumption or sudden breakdowns can be directly caused by what they put in the tank.
In this chapter, we’ll explain how to tell that you’ve filled up with poor-quality petrol or diesel, and what the short-term and long-term consequences can be.
#### 1) Unstable idle and fluctuating revs
This is one of the most common symptoms of poor-quality fuel.
The engine:
- idles unevenly,
- revs “jump” up and down irregularly,
- may start vibrating more than usual.
Why does this happen? Poor-quality fuels contain less stable components that burn less well, or they may be contaminated with water or biocomponents.
This is also typical of injectors clogged by long-term use of poor-quality fuel.
#### 2) Engine jerking when pulling away
If, after filling up, the engine:
- jerks,
- responds more slowly to the throttle,
- loses smoothness,
it may indicate fuel:
- with a low level of additives,
- containing water,
- that burns unevenly (low octane/cetane number).
Jerking is often the result of:
- insufficient lubricity,
- the presence of paraffin wax (in the winter variant),
- a poor biocomponent.
#### 3) Loss of power and slower engine response
When fuel burns poorly, the engine:
- doesn’t “pull” as well,
- responds more slowly to the throttle,
- loses power under load (e.g. when overtaking),
- vibrates more.
This symptom usually appears within the first 20 kilometres after filling up.
#### 4) Increased fuel consumption
Poor-quality fuel usually has:
- a lower energy content,
- a poorer air/fuel mixture,
- a higher biocomponent content,
- poorer combustion properties.
As a result, the engine uses more fuel to deliver the same performance.
Consumption rises by 0.5 to 1.5 litres per 100 km, sometimes even more.
#### 5) Starting problems
If, after filling up, the car:
- is harder to start,
- only starts at the second attempt,
- cranks for a long time before it catches,
it is a strong indicator of poor-quality fuel.
Most often this is due to poor additives or the biocomponent content.
The problem tends to be:
- low lubricity,
- water in the fuel,
- in winter, a poor winter variant.
#### 6) Black or white smoke from the exhaust
Exhaust smoke can tell you a lot:
- black smoke → poor combustion of the mixture (poor-quality fuel)
- white smoke → water in the fuel / condensation of the biocomponent
- blue smoke → an oil problem (often unrelated, but it can be linked to poor-quality fuel)
#### 7) Noisier engine running
If the engine is noticeably noisier than usual, it may be because the fuel:
- is detonating (low-octane petrol),
- has a low cetane number (diesel),
- contains impurities.
Modern engines are very sensitive to combustion stability.
#### 8) Water in fuel: the silent engine killer
Water in fuel can cause:
- injector corrosion,
- clogged filters,
- performance problems,
- engine jerking,
- failure to start.
It occurs mainly in diesel, as the biocomponent attracts moisture.
Water in fuel is one of the worst scenarios that can happen when you fill up.
#### 9) Microbial contamination (“diesel bug”) in diesel
Diesel tanks sometimes suffer from microbial growth. This “slime” can cause:
- blocked filters,
- impaired injection,
- high servicing costs.
Good stations clean their tanks regularly; cheaper ones often don’t.
#### 10) Long-term problems and the risk of expensive repairs
Using poor-quality fuel over the long term causes:
- faster engine wear,
- clogged injectors,
- noisy running,
- higher consumption,
- ignition faults,
- problems with the diesel particulate filter (DPF),
- costly repairs (sometimes running into tens of thousands of crowns).
- injector cleaning: 3,000 to 15,000 CZK
- injector replacement: 6,000 to 20,000 CZK per injector
- high-pressure pump repair: 10,000 to 35,000 CZK
- clogged DPF filter: 6,000 to 30,000 CZK
1. Keep an eye on how the engine behaves.
1. If problems appear → top up with quality fuel.
1. An injector cleaning additive can also help.
1. If the problems are serious, take the car to a garage.
But the best approach is prevention:
Fill up at verified fuel stations, exactly the ones PHMarket selects.
### 6. Fuel quality at PHMarket: How we select partner fuel stations
Fuel quality isn’t a marketing slogan; it is the very reason PHMarket was created. We don’t want to be just another “discount app” that signs up fuel stations indiscriminately. Quite the opposite. Our goal is to build a nationwide loyalty programme based on a combination of two key values:
#### 1) Quality fuel
#### 2) Fair prices for drivers
To be able to guarantee this, we have to be very strict about who we let into the programme.
#### 1) Careful selection of fuel stations
Every fuel station that wants to become a PHMarket partner must meet several key criteria:
The station must consistently source quality petrol and diesel from verified suppliers. We aren’t looking for the cheapest fuel; we’re looking for reliable, quality fuel that doesn’t cause engine problems.
We check:
- the condition of the underground tanks
- maintenance of the fuel dispensers
- filtration
- fuel turnover
- technological standards
The station must be able to provide clean, stable and technically flawless fuel.
#### 2) A focus on quality diesel without unnecessary biocomponents
For many drivers, it is essential to have access to diesel:
- with a quality biocomponent,
- or with no biocomponent at all,
- with high lubricity,
- with a high cetane number,
- that is also suitable for winter driving.
Many unbranded stations work with very high-quality diesel suppliers, and that is exactly why PHMarket brings them together in one programme.
#### 3) A fair approach to customers
PHMarket works with fuel stations that:
- have fair prices,
- communicate transparently,
- don’t try to “claw back their margin” at the expense of quality,
- care about service and the overall standard of their operation.
We don’t want to be just a tech app; we want to be a guarantee of reliability.
### Conclusion: Quality fuel = lower costs, better performance and peace of mind on the road
Quality fuel isn’t a luxury. It is the foundation of running a car reliably and economically.
That’s why at PHMarket we’ve created a programme that makes life easier for drivers: one app → quality fuel → a fair discount.
You no longer have to worry about whether you’re filling up in the right place. We’ve selected vetted fuel stations that meet our quality standards, so you can fill up both cheaper and smarter.

Most drivers fill up wherever it happens to “work out”, or rely on old loyalty cards. Yet there is a way to save hundreds of crowns on every tank without compromising on fuel quality. With two fill-ups a month, that adds up to 400 to 500 CZK or more, money you could have put towards something far more enjoyable.

#### The app’s main pillars:
- A simple discount system: No need to wash your car or buy a coffee... Everyone simply gets a discount
